description.narrative: According to Cadre Harmonisé in March 2022, 1,215,625 people are in need of food assistance in Tillabéri. 306,853 people in Ouallamand 114,120 people in Ayorou are affected by this shortfall, caused by low cereal production (SAP 2021). Food provision remains a concern in all départements in the region. The closure of a number of markets has disrupted the function of the local market, the price of food items have risen by between 22.2% and 45.7%, and available volumes are at risk of falling in the coming months. FewsNet (December 2021) forecasts that prices will remain above average for the rest of the year, faced with growing demand and falling output. However, according to the Oxfam MSNA survey from January 2022, 64% of host households in Tillabéri report that their main food source is from their own production, while 30% primarily purchase food at markets. However, 57% of IDPs depend on markets, and 36% on humanitarian aid, to meet their food needs, while 24% of refugees purchase food at markets (MSNA Survey, Oxfam 2022) In the regions of Tillabéri, Maradi and Tahoua, the MSNA Survey showed that about 93% of those surveyed believed that their current food stock is not enough to get through to the next harvest. More than half (55%) had enough to last less than a month and just 5% had enough to last more than three months. The main reasons for the lack of food were: poor harvest/no harvest (65%), high price of food (58%), lossof income (36%). Tillabéri recorded a shortfall of 4,369,415 tonnes of solids (OCHA 2021), the highest of any region in Niger. The départements of Banibangou, Tillabéri and Ouallam are most vulnerable to this situation. Pastoral households report that the level of insecurity is limiting their access to grazing land; the theft of livestock, rising grain prices with unfavourable terms, the highprice of livestock feed and the closure of some cattle markets are some of the effects experienced by pastoral households in affected areas. In Ouallam, 70% of those surveyed have adopted stress management strategies, while 20% have adopted crisis management. Irrigation has become an increasing challenge in grazing lands, due to the lack of pastoral water points, rapid drying of surface waterpoints and dilapidated facilities. Between 55% and 86% of rural households in Tillabéri use containers with no covers to carry water. At sites that were visited, young women reported a need for access to soap. Such access is important for the menstrual hygiene ofwomen and girls. This need also reflects the vulnerable position of women, due to their lack of funds. With respect to protection, the target area faces a number of risk factors, including a worsening security situation in localities along the border with Mali and Burkina Faso; limited or no access to localities affected by GANE attacks; high pressure on resources (e.g. land, water, housing) and the resultant risk of inter-community conflict; and an insufficient humanitarian response in border communities under threat from GANEs. Between 1 January and 31 December 2021, 645 civilians were killed in 318 security incidents, an increase of 200% on 2020. Insecurity places a major strain on essential social services; the disruption has forced 680 schools and 34 medical centres to close. At the stakeholder synergy and local coordination meeting, attended by OCHA, UNHCR, MAH/GC (Ministry for Humanitarian Action) and Oxfam, it was noted that new internally displaced persons at the Ouallam have not yet received assistance following the aid received under the RRMs. Sporadic population movements have increased significantly, with waves of migration continuing to occur in a number of départements inthe region. Between October and November 2021, 2,283 households, or 20,000 internally displaced persons, fled attacks and incidents. 921 Malian refugees have arrived since the beginning of attacks in the Gao region of Mali, ongoing since midFebruary, while 13,737 refugees have arrived from Burkina Faso. More than 1,000 households have arrived from villages in Mali during March 2022 (OCHA 2022).

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novibs main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fund raising, campaigning and advocacy. The Hub Niamey Niger exists since 2006 as a humanitarian field office and since 2012 as the decentralized Country office for Oxfam Novib, dealing with all the development and humanitarian themes like Sustainable livelihoods, Right to Basic services, Humanitarian and resilience interventions, The right to be heard and the right to an Identity, including women's rights and sexual and reproductive health rights. The Country Office in Niger works with local partners to realize the vision of a Niger without poverty
